# Getting started

This chapter takes a reader from a fresh clone to regenerated figures and
tables. It covers what to install, the two ways to reproduce the paper, and a
short tour of the package so that the later chapters have a map to point at.

## Requirements

The package was built and checked on R 4.6; **R \(\ge\) 4.5** is required. The
setup script enforces this and stops on older versions.

- **Track B** (figures and tables) needs only CRAN packages used by the
  reporting scripts and this book. No Stan, no `svyder`, no restricted data.
- **Track A** (full recomputation) additionally needs **CmdStan (\(\ge\) 2.35)**
  through `cmdstanr` and the `svyder` package, because the models are fit with
  Stan and the application calls the production diagnostic API.
- **LaTeX** is optional. The reporting scripts write `.tex` tables to
  `output/tables/`; you need a LaTeX installation only if you want to typeset
  those tables into a PDF. The numbers themselves are also written to `.csv`.

## Installing dependencies

The setup script is `code/00_setup.R`. It defaults to the public Track B path.
Run it once from the package root:

```r
source("code/00_setup.R")
```

The script:

1. checks the R version (\(\ge\) 4.5) and stops otherwise;
2. installs and loads the CRAN packages needed by Track B reporting and book
   rendering;
3. skips `cmdstanr`, CmdStan, and `svyder` in the default Track B path;
4. sets up the project paths and a master seed, and prints `sessionInfo()`.

For Track A, opt in explicitly before sourcing the same script:

```r
Sys.setenv(SVYDER_TRACK = "A")
source("code/00_setup.R")
```

Track A adds the from-scratch dependencies: `cmdstanr`, CmdStan, extra CRAN
packages such as `posterior`, and `svyder` from GitHub. The `svyder` package
implements the production diagnostic API; its documentation is at
[joonho112.github.io/svyder](https://joonho112.github.io/svyder/).

## The two tracks

Both tracks reproduce the paper's numbers exactly. They differ only in where
they start.

| | Track A --- full recomputation | Track B --- figures and tables |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **Starts from** | raw / synthetic data | shipped precomputed results |
| **Simulation** | regenerates all 4,800 replications on synthetic data (HPC recommended for the full grid) | reads the shipped per-replication files and summary |
| **Application** | fits the NSECE model; needs the restricted-use data (ICPSR 38445) and Stan | reads the shipped model fit |
| **Requires** | R, CmdStan, `svyder`, and (application only) restricted data | R plus CRAN packages |
| **Time** | many hours for the simulation; a couple of hours for the NSECE fit | minutes on a laptop |

The simulation is not merely reproducible but **bit-for-bit** reproducible from
the seeds: each replication draws its data from a deterministic per-cell,
per-replication seed, so a Track A rerun regenerates the shipped files exactly.
[The pipeline chapter](04-simulation-pipeline.qmd) shows where that seed comes
from. Track B is the default entry point and is what this guide is written
from.

## Track B quick start

From the package root, or after opening `svyder-replication.Rproj` in RStudio,
three lines regenerate everything:

```r
source("code/00_setup.R")                        # one-time Track B setup
source("code/03_results/results_01_theory.R")    # Figure 1
source("code/03_results/results_02_aggregate.R") # Figures 2-4, Tables 2-5
```

Outputs land in `output/figures/` (PDF and PNG) and `output/tables/` (LaTeX and
CSV). `results_02_aggregate.R` reads the shipped per-replication files and the
shipped NSECE fit; it fits no models and reads no restricted data. It also
prints an integrity summary that re-derives the paper's headline quantities as
it goes, so a successful run is self-checking.

::: {.callout-note}
The reporting scripts read only files that ship with the package. Track B
therefore runs on a laptop with no Stan toolchain and no data-use agreement.
:::

## A tour of the repository

The layout separates the two studies (simulation and application), the raw
compute from the reporting, and the shipped results from the code that
produces them.

```
svyder-replication/
├── code/
│   ├── 00_setup.R                 track-aware setup (Track B default)
│   ├── 01_simulation/             build the 4,800 replications (Track A)
│   │   ├── sim_00_config.R         the 24-cell factorial design and the seeds
│   │   ├── sim_01_dgp.R            two-stage informative-sampling data generator
│   │   ├── sim_02_fit.R            fit the weighted HLR in Stan; convergence gate
│   │   ├── sim_03_postprocess.R    sandwich variance, DER, coverage per replication
│   │   ├── sim_04_run_single.R     one replication end to end
│   │   └── sim_05_run_batch.R      parallel CLI driver over the whole grid
│   ├── 02_application/            the NSECE 2019 analysis (Track A; restricted data)
│   │   ├── app_01_prepare_data.R   build the model-ready arrays from the extract
│   │   ├── app_02_fit_refit.R      fit the model, dual-target DER
│   │   └── app_03_der_supplement.R weight-convention sensitivity and factors R_k
│   ├── 03_results/               regenerate the figures and tables (Track B)
│   │   ├── results_01_theory.R     Figure 1 (closed-form DER curves)
│   │   └── results_02_aggregate.R  Figures 2-4 and Tables 2-5
│   └── helpers/                   self-contained DER / sandwich / plotting code
├── stan/
│   └── hlr_weighted.stan          weighted hierarchical logistic regression
├── data/
│   ├── DATA_ACCESS.md             how to obtain the restricted NSECE data
│   └── precomputed/              shipped, non-identifiable results for Track B
│       ├── simulation/            per-cell simulation summary
│       └── application/           NSECE model fit and supplement
├── output/
│   ├── simulation/               the 4,800 per-replication files (shipped)
│   ├── figures/                   regenerated figures land here
│   └── tables/                    regenerated tables land here
└── book/                         this guide
```

Two conventions are worth noting for reading the later chapters. The
per-replication files under `output/simulation/` are the granular Track A
output, one small `.rds` per replication; the `data/precomputed/` directory
holds the compact, non-identifiable summaries that Track B reads. And the code
is numbered in dependency order within each folder, so `sim_00` through `sim_05`
is exactly the order in which a replication flows.
